constructiveClusters.story: UK Court Overturns Trinidad and Tobago Anti-Gay Sex Law
constructiveClusters.summary: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London unanimously struck down Trinidad and Tobago's colonial-era Sexual Offences Act criminalizing consensual same-sex relations between men, concluding an 11-year legal challenge brought by dual-citizen activist Jason Jones. briefing.whatsNext: The ruling takes immediate legal effect within Trinidad and Tobago's domestic jurisdiction, forcing local law enforcement agencies and prosecutors to drop active enforcement of the invalidated provisions. The outcome hinges on whether domestic religious and political groups mount nationalist backlashes against the Privy Council or attempt legislative workarounds to restrict broader LGBTQ+ rights.
